rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so the table pushes obfuscation upward while respecting that this is a hot-loop floating-point benchmark suite (flops/fbench/whetstone dominate) where control-flow transforms pay a heavy per-iteration price. SUB stays the highest-weighted pass: instruction substitution is cheap in both time and size and is especially effective against the arithmetic-heavy FP code, so it can be applied broadly. IBR and ICALL are raised as the mid-cost structural diversifiers — indirect branches and indirect calls obscure the call/branch graph at acceptable overhead for the small function set (16 functions, tiny text). FLA and BCF keep high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so the selector applies them selectively rather than globally, protecting the innermost numeric loops while still allowing flattening/bogus-control-flow on colder functions like main and schedule. SPLIT is kept as a low-cost helper that enlarges basic-block diversity for FLA/IBR to work with, and IGV stays moderate since global state in this program is limited but worth diversifying. CorrectnessRisk values remain modest across the board since round 1 showed clean compilation and execution, permitting slightly more aggressive selection without threatening correctness.
